recipes.name: Porcupine Meatballs
ingredients_raw: 1 cup low-sodium chicken stock, or more as needed

steps.text: Mix ground beef, rice, water, onion, salt, celery salt, garlic powder, and black pepper thoroughly in a bowl until well combined. Roll mixture into 12 meatballs.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Place meatballs into the hot skillet; cook, turning once halfway through cooking, until well browned, about 8 minutes. Drain and discard excess grease.

Pour tomato sauce, chicken stock, Worcestershire sauce, and sugar into the skillet; reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and simmer until meatballs are no longer pink in the center and rice is tender, about 45 minutes. Stir in more stock if sauce becomes too dry.

raw_recipe.headline: Porcupine Meatballs
raw_recipe.description: These porcupine meatballs made with ground beef and onion and filled with little rice "spikes" are simmered on the stovetop in a simple tomato sauce.

video.description: These are fun meatballs because the rice gets cooked from the inside and then pokes out! Perfect as an appetizer or for a side to your meal.

review.reviewBody: Only 4 stars, as is.... But I modified to our family's taste and they became a 5 star. I think there was a tad too much water... the mixture was too loose. So I added an egg. I also added some worcesteshire to the meat mixture and eliminated the celery salt. I used 2 packages of dried onion soup mix to make a gravy. I make patties , not balls and once the patties (6 generous ones) were browned, I added the soup mixture (dry soup mix, water and flour) to the pan and let it cook 30-45 minutes. Served it with mashed potatoes and watched my family devour it. No leftovers. We like the brown gravy better than the tomato sauce. This is how my mom made it when we were kids in the 50's. Only no onion soup mix ...she made the gravy from scratch...

I’m sorry but this recipe would yield a bland fall apart meatball that is crunchy inside. Where is the flavoring in this? I watched and learned from my mom over 60 years ago and she made the best Porcupine -Meatballs ever. It isn’t difficult at all. Here is my recipe changes for the one in this article that will add some life and flavor to these. 1. I personally like to use both pork sausage and ground beef. 50/50 is good. More specifically I prefer to use the Jimmy Dean hot sausage to mix with my hamburger. 2. Put some flavor in it. Try adding a little Italian seasoning (1/2 to 1 tsp). The same goes for a little bit of garlic powder and onion powder. 3. Very important. Make sure that the chopped onion is very finely chopped. I use a processor to make it that way. This will insure that the meatballs don’t fall apart during the browning and subsequent cooking process. 4. Do not use regular rice but instead use Minute Rice. This will prevent the crunchy undercooked effect of long grain rice. 5. My mother used to make a sauce that was very similar to her spaghetti sauce using the tomato sauce and the ingredients listed above BUT in today’s world we have packaged spaghetti sauces. Use one of these and it will call for that can of tomato sauce that is part of the recipe here. 6. I understand the concept of a low sodium broth but then this recipe has 2 different salts in it. Why? Use a good chicken bullion to make the broth and eliminate the other 2 salts. 7. For those who don’t like to add sugar to cut the acidity try adding a tiny squirt of lemon juice instead. Try these changes and apply them to this recipe and see how you like it then. I’m sure you’ll approve of the results but if you don’t then go ahead and make the bland version.

I can’t speak for the method of cooking these because we grew up with these made in a stovetop pressure cooker. My mom always used tomato soup and water for the sauce, which we used as a gravy on mashed potatoes - sounds gross but it’s delicious. I bought a Cuisinart electric pressure cooker several years ago (before InstaPots became so popular) and I’ve always used it for these but the meatballs just lacked something. The addition of the celery salt and the Worcestershire was just the ticket. I also soak the rice in an equal amount of water for about 15 minutes before adding the beef and seasonings and I always use a lean ground beef so the meatballs hold their shape in the cooker.

We have had a version of this porcupines for our family since I was a kid… we cooked our in the pressure cooker and used diluted cream of mushroom soup instead of tomato sauce and worcestershire. We loved them…

I did adjust this recipe by doubling the sauce so I'd have enough sauce for spaghetti, and using minute rice to ensure complete cooking. I also added a 10 oz. can of V8 juice and two tbsp of flour to the sauce for thickener. I then put all in a crockpot and cooked on low for four hours. (My crockpot does run hot, so might need to add an hour if yours doesn't and you want to try this method). I'm cooking for two and this is a great recipe to freeze in dishes for two. The flavor is all about the sauce and you can adjust to suit your particular taste. I think this would be good with parmesan cheese, as well. Very tasty and versatile recipe.

I've been making porcupine meatballs for years. You can also make them in a slo-cooker. I've never made them on top of stove. I usually do them in the oven. My recipe calls for tomato soup rather than tomato sauce .

Well…I did a completely difference sauce. I made a maranara sauce. Also where water was listed, I used chicken broth. I used basmati rice to mix in with the meatballs. I might have simmered for an hour. The rice was cooked perfectly. The meat was moist (I did stir things every 8-15 mins and basted them with the sauce. And I let the rolled meatballs sit for a few hours before cooking. Also served over gaba rice. It was outstanding!

My mom used cream of mushroom soup + 1 can of water in place of tomato sauce mixture, and cooked in pressure cooker for 15 minutes. Although I still cherish her 1945 Presto Cooker, I use my InstaPot. Your exact recipe is in the 1940’s Presto Cookbook. (Along with Braised Squirrel!)

OMG, I have been making these for almost 30 years. Made it while the kids were still home and still making it for the two of us in retirement. Currently (sans kids) I make up a batch of the mixture, then scoop the meatballs onto a sheet pan and freeze. The next day I then (because of our eating habits), I freeze four of the meatballs using freezer sealing meal into individual bags. Easy to pull a bag and make quick meal. I usually cover for 45 minutes, uncover, add Mozzarella for another 10-15 minutes uncovered. Of course I add more garlic and my personal seasonings. I add a bunch of chopped onion, a dab of Ketchup, Worcestershire and other favorite seasonings. I also add shaved carrots, or those shreds you can purchase if you like. Depending on how big a batch, one or two eggs. Think meatloaf, but with Instant Rice instead of bread crumbs.

This is a basic recipe to build on for your tastes. I've been eating and making them my whole life, although my recipe calls for a green pepper. I've found the trick is to put the onion and green pepper into the food processor, make a slurry to which you add the seasonings. Then add the rice so it starts to soak up the flavors. Let it sit just a short while, then add the meat. Roll and Bake them on a cookie sheet in the oven to do more at a time and avoid the splatter mess. I make huge batches of these (like 10+ lbs of burger) because they freeze beautifully. Just place the meatballs in pan with tomato sauce/water or tomato juice, quick meal for busy night. You don't even have to thaw them if you make sure to add extra time to the simmer step. You can also put them into a pressure pan with the juice but be careful to have plenty of room so it doesn't foam out of the vents. Even quicker week night meal!

I really like this recipe because it is the one my Mom used back in the day! It is identical to the one in the old Betty Crocker cook books and it even has the too large amount of water that makes the meatballs so loose. I cut the amount of water down to a 1/4 cup, subbed in for the Cream of Tomato Soup for the tomato sauce and I soak the rice in water for 15 minutes to get them ready to cook faster, otherwise they come out a bit more al dente than I like. I really should try it w instant rice instead. Using a full 30 ounces of soup helped the rice cook softer. I gently turn the meatballs when I uncover them after 45 minutes in the oven. I think my Mom shredded old bread and added it to the meatballs but I am not sure she did it all the time or how it changed the rest of the recipe. 
Sometimes I add either 1 Tbs Calabrian chili sauce or a teaspoon of Mediterranean Mix spices to give it a different taste. 
This is a fun recipe to play with!
Horrible! I followed the receipe exactly and the rice didn't cook. Crunchy meatballs with not much flavor. Threw them away :(
Best ones yet
Very good with rice. I made the meatballs smaller to cut down the cooking time.
These were so good. I made the meatballs a day ahead and browned and cookedthem the next day. Very flavorful. I served them over cabbage and onions. This will be in our regular meal rotation.
This was literally one of the very first recipes in my 8th grade Home Ec. Class. So delicious and we felt like real cooks. Brought tears to my eyes.
I made these growing up and lost the recipe over time. They are absolutely delicious.
My mom after browning the meatballs would finish cooking them in a pressure cooker. This cause the rice to stick out of the meatballs like porcupine. Quills

I love stuffed bell peppers. My children did not. I would cut a few peppers in 1/2 and fill with the porcupine mixture. I didnt pan fry the meatballs before filling the peppers but I imagine it would work fine. Put the filled peppers along side the porcupine meatballs and bake like usual. Everyone was happy.

I made the recipe as written. I omitted the salt because there is already a lot of salt in tinned tomato sauce, celery salt. The flavour was good. BUT There is too much water in the meat mixture. The meatballs basically melted in the fry pan while browning and I ended up getting small patties instead of balls. I will make it again, but next time I will omit the water and substitute a well beaten egg instead, to hold the meatballs together better.
